correctness.rationale: For each specified set of surviving leaves, exactly its cardinality among previously born labels counts forbidden insertion gaps. Multiplying the conditional probabilities yields the exact joint product. A paired-to-product ratio factors as 1−1/(4k²); logarithmic asymptotics and an explicit n|Cov|≤1/2 bound justify every age-rescaled Riemann sum. Direct integrations give K. Complete independent Stirling-permutation vs plane-tree enumeration through seven birth labels and 528 exact assertions corroborate, but do not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: A natural age-indexed question in preferential attachment is which birth cohorts remain leaves and how their random counts cofluctuate. The explicit two-variable age covariance K(s,t), plus arbitrary bounded age-weight covariance functional, gives all age-window second-order limits, not only a sign or the previously known total variance \(n/9\). The joint survival factorization supplies finite-size interpretable probabilities. The result does not pretend to be a Gaussian functional limit or an independent certification.
